title: Kernel Constitution — machine-readable mirror
note: This file mirrors docs/architecture/KERNEL-CONSTITUTION.md. On any disagreement, the markdown document is authoritative (SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md: docs/architecture ranks with ADR-elaborating documents; this JSON is a compiled projection of it, not an independent record). Synthesis, not new decision — zero new ADRs required to produce either file.

kernel_primitives.fixed_until: a proven dependency-cut requires an 11th (docs/architecture/PACKAGE-MAP.md package-creation rule, applied identically to primitives)
kernel_primitives.everything_else_is: adapter or higher layer, never kernel — see non_goals

1_state_machine_algebra.note: No prior ADR defines the transition algebra itself; ADR-0009/0010/0011 assume a state machine exists.

elements.name: State
elements.definition: An immutable snapshot of everything a Run needs to resume. Never partial — either fully resumable or not a State (in-flight work that hasn't reached one yet).

elements.name: Event
elements.definition: An input that may cause a transition. Carries its own identity so duplicate/replayed events are detectable.

elements.name: Context
elements.definition: Data available to a Guard/Action at transition time, distinct from State. May include ambient information (current time, external system status) not itself persisted as part of State.

elements.name: Guard
elements.definition: A pure, deterministic predicate over (State, Event, Context) deciding whether a transition is legal. Never has side effects.

elements.name: Transition
elements.definition: (State, Event) -> State, mediated by zero or more Guards, producing zero or more Action/Effect records.

elements.name: Action/Effect
elements.definition: What a transition causes — may be purely internal (another kernel state change) or may dispatch an Operation (see section 2).

elements.name: Error
elements.definition: A transition a Guard rejects is not a kernel failure — a defined, expected outcome ('illegal transition'), mapped in the adversarial matrix.

elements.name: Cancellation
elements.definition: An explicit Event type; a cancelled Run reaches a defined terminal State, never simply stops emitting Events.

elements.name: Completion
elements.definition: A terminal State from which no further Event causes a Transition (checked, not assumed).

elements.name: Replay
elements.definition: Re-deriving State from a persisted Event log must produce byte-identical State to what was actually persisted, or the determinism invariant is violated.

1_state_machine_algebra.determinism_invariant: same state + same event + same deterministic input => same transition result
1_state_machine_algebra.illegal_by_construction_rule: A Transition function that reads any non-deterministic source (wall-clock time, random state, network I/O) directly is a defect, not a style violation. Non-determinism enters only through Context, which is itself part of the recorded input to a Transition, never invisible to it.

2_operation_side_effect_state_machine.note: The exact state enum ADR-0011 established the need for but did not itself enumerate.

operation_fields.name: IdempotencyKey
operation_fields.purpose: what the external system uses to detect a duplicate, where it supports one

operation_fields.name: InputHash
operation_fields.purpose: detects a caller reusing an OperationID with different input — must be rejected, not silently accepted

operation_fields.name: PolicyDecision
operation_fields.purpose: the recorded outcome of policy evaluation (section 4)

2_operation_side_effect_state_machine.core_rule: A timeout is never automatically converted into a failure for a non-idempotent external effect. DISPATCHED transitions to UNKNOWN_OUTCOME, not REJECTED, when the caller cannot confirm what happened. REJECTED means positive evidence the effect did not occur; UNKNOWN_OUTCOME means the kernel does not know. Collapsing the two is the failure mode this primitive exists to prevent.
2_operation_side_effect_state_machine.reconciling_rule: RECONCILING must query the external system's own record of what it did (an idempotent status check, where supported) before ever re-dispatching. A capability with no such status check degrades RECONCILING's only exit to MANUAL_REVIEW — a legitimate, expected outcome, not a defect.

evidence_this_phase.reason: no real capability/side-effect implementation exists yet (Phase 8/9 unstarted)

3_durability.checkpoint_boundary: A Checkpoint is a (State, sequence number, schema version) tuple, written atomically — partial checkpoint writes must never be observable by a subsequent reader.
3_durability.persistence_ordering: Checkpoints for a single Run are totally ordered by sequence number. Cross-Run ordering is not guaranteed unless a Run explicitly depends on another's Checkpoint (open question, STORE-INTERFACES.md section 19).
3_durability.recovery: On restart, the kernel loads the highest-sequence Checkpoint for a Run and resumes from there — never from partially-written state (verified this phase, scope-qualified, by E5-DURABLE-RESTART).
3_durability.replay: Recovering State from Checkpoint + subsequent Event log entries must satisfy the section-1 determinism invariant exactly.
3_durability.duplicate_suppression: Resuming a Run must not re-execute an Operation already DISPATCHED before the crash — this is where section 2's UNKNOWN_OUTCOME/RECONCILING states and section 3's checkpoint/recovery model meet directly; recovery alone cannot resolve this, reconciliation must.

crash_semantics.rule: A crash at any point must leave the persisted state in exactly one of two observable conditions: the pre-crash Checkpoint (if the in-flight write never completed) or the post-write Checkpoint (if it did) — never anything in between.

3_durability.schema_migration: A Checkpoint written by version N must remain readable by version N+1 (STORE-INTERFACES.md invariant 4), tested against real persisted checkpoints, never synthetic fixtures built to match the new shape.

concurrency.minimum: StateStore writes for a single Run require optimistic concurrency at minimum

4_capability_policy.formula: WHO + CAN + DO WHAT + TO WHICH OBJECT + UNDER WHICH CONDITIONS + UNTIL WHEN + BECAUSE OF WHICH GRANT (WHY)

capability.answers: is this principal (Identity) permitted this action on this object at all
capability.shape: a grant, with an expiry, traceable to its issuing authority

policy.answers: is this action permitted right now, given environment/risk/cost/data-sensitivity/network conditions
policy.evaluation: independent of capability, deterministic, enforceable without a model in the loop

4_capability_policy.separation_rule: Capability and Policy are kept separate and both independently enforceable, never merged into one check and never delegated to model judgement.
4_capability_policy.enforcement_point: source-to-sink, at the point an Operation actually dispatches (section 2) — never at the point a model produces or receives text. A check that only runs against model output is advisory, not this primitive.

5_evidence_verdict.note: Formalizes the E0-E5 evidence-hierarchy discipline used informally throughout this repository's research as an explicit kernel primitive for the first time.
evidence_fields: provenance (what produced it — a Transition, an Operation dispatch, a reconciliation query)
transition linkage (which State change it is evidence for)
authorization linkage (which PolicyDecision/Capability grant it is evidence for, where applicable)

verdict_lifecycle.note: Same five labels this phase's own final receipt uses, deliberately — a Verdict at kernel level and a claim label at documentation level are the same concept applied at different scales, not two different vocabularies.
verdict_lifecycle.malformed_if: a Verdict with no cited Evidence records

layers.does_not_own: Execution mechanics, model calls, tool implementations

layers.owns: observe -> interpret -> propose -> validate -> authorize -> execute -> observe result -> update state -> continue/stop
layers.does_not_own: Planning as an inseparable primitive — a loop may be planning-free

layers.owns: Multi-step orchestration with explicit control flow; may host an AgentLoop as one of its steps
layers.does_not_own: Being required for an AgentLoop to function — a loop never needs to 'become' a workflow

layers.owns: A Workflow pause point, checkpointed exactly like any other durable pause (ADR-0015)
Model calls, tool execution, MCP/A2A protocol translation, sandbox isolation
layers.does_not_own: Kernel semantics — an adapter translates, it never redefines what Operation/Capability/Evidence mean

invariants: The model never authorizes its own proposals.
The kernel never executes directly — it validates and hands off to Runtime.
Runtime never decides policy — it executes what Policy already authorized.

non_goals.note: Each has a real, planned home (PACKAGE-MAP.md, BOUNDARY-RECONCILIATION.md); none may leak kernel-shaped assumptions into its own design (same rule already applied to MCP in ADR-0009).

testability.rule: Every element in sections 1-6 must correspond to at least one case in .context/scenarios/kernel-core.json's adversarial matrix, marked EXECUTED, SIMULATED, or NOT_EXECUTED with a stated reason. A primitive with no corresponding test case is not yet a tested part of this constitution, regardless of how precisely it is described in prose.
